description.narrative: The project is implemented in the Philippines. The main outcome areas it contributes to are Countering the threats to democracy and human rights and advancing equality and worker's rights. The main rights holders are the labour educators and shop stewards within the partner unions and partner cooperatives of LEARN. Through educational module development, trainings and research the project aims to achieve that LEARN increases its relevance to its partners and contributes to the strenghtening of the Philippine labor movement.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Labor Education and Research Network, LEARN and The Workers' Educational Association (ABF). LEARN was founded in 1986, and has been an important contributing factor in the consolidation of the labor movement in the Philippines. ABF has extensive experience as a provider and developer of popular education in Sweden and is also very active internationally.Other Donors to the OrganisationThere are no other donors to the project. Besides OPC, LEARN receives funds from German Trade Union Confederation DGB-BW, SASK through IDWF, and Friedrich Ebert Stiftung-FES.Project ObjectivePartner unions and cooperatives are better managed and have increased capacity to defend and advance rights and interests of the workers, and are helping to improve their lives The LEARN Research Institute presents workers' narratives and analysis of economic and labor market trends that engage labor unions and workers cooperative in conversations, debates, and actions.Actor groupsThe main actors within decision-makers" are the The Department of Labor and Employment, National Anti-Poverty Commission, Department of trade and Industry and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority. Within "actors working in cooperation" the main actors are the trade union confederation SENTRO (Sentro ng Nagkakaisa at Progresibong Manggagawa), The Philippine Cooperative Center and NAGKAISA, the country's largest coalition of labor unions, federations and centers. For the actor group "rightholders" the main actors are the labour educators and shop stewards within the partner unions and partner cooperatives of LEARN."
